criteria.quote: An itchy sleeping nose means Drowzee is eating dreams.
criteria.revision: Replace the first line with: “An itchy nose while you sleep is a sure sign Drowzee is standing above your pillow—trying to eat your dream through your nostrils.” This uses the research’s stranger, more specific image immediately.

criteria.quote: Its twitching nose can find sleepers and their dreams.
What connects one itchy nose to a dream Drowzee eats?
criteria.revision: Make the open loop more investigative: “How does Drowzee get from finding a sleeping person to finding—and eating—their dream?” This preserves the unanswered mechanism instead of restating the premise.

criteria.quote: Its twitching nose can find sleepers and their dreams.
criteria.revision: Separate the discoveries so each scene advances: change the second scene to “When its nose twitches, Drowzee can tell where someone is sleeping,” then let the next scene reveal, “It can also tell what that person is dreaming about.”

criteria.quote: Drowzee remembers every dream it eats and sometimes shows them later.
criteria.revision: Add the missing conditions to sharpen the reveal: “Drowzee remembers every dream it eats. If you sleep by it all the time, it may show you one it ate before.”

criteria.quote:
THE DREAM ISN'T HIDDEN

THE PATH GOES THROUGH YOUR NOSE

DREAM THEFT FROM ABOVE
criteria.revision: Give the middle section a new dimension by replacing one repeated nose-and-dream beat with: “It rarely eats adult dreams—children’s are much tastier.” Then use the nostril detail as the physical climax.

criteria.quote: The whole trap clicks: Drowzee's nose finds the sleeper, then its nostrils lead to the dream.
criteria.revision: End with a consequence that goes beyond restating the route: “And if you think you had a good dream but can’t remember it, Drowzee probably ate it.”

criteria.quote: Is dream-eating Drowzee clever, or too creepy to trust?
criteria.revision: Replace it with a split grounded in the research: “Would you want Drowzee to show you a dream it ate—or would you rather keep your dreams?”
